headline: High risk of cascading errors and compliance leakage if Khoj outputs are fed into social-auto-upload without verification; shared broad egress raises additional leakage and conflict concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed personal notes/files and social-auto-upload consumes local media files and CLI inputs, so a manual copy-paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions. However, no shared clipboard, MCP, or direct parser bridge is documented, so the pathway is limited and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Khoj-generated text into social-auto-upload inputs without review, injection is possible.
IF either agent begins parsing shared files as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Review any copied text before pasting into the uploader.
Keep Khoj notes and upload manifests in separate folders.
Use a plain-text staging file with manual diff review.
Disable any auto-import or auto-run wrapper around the uploader.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while social-auto-upload handles account data plus media files. Both have broad network egress, so if either sends retrieved content to external services, sensitive notes or media metadata can leave the local boundary in default use. No isolation or DLP is documented.
conditions: IF Khoj retrieves personal notes that are then pasted or exported into social-auto-upload workflows, leakage occurs.
IF social-auto-upload uploads media or account data to third-party APIs, those contents may leave the workspace.
mitigations: Store sensitive notes outside the upload workspace.
Use a test account with non-sensitive media.
Inspect outbound destinations before running either agent.
Turn off optional cloud/search integrations in Khoj when handling secrets.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem or modify git state, so direct destructive write-write conflict is blocked. The main overlap is read access in Khoj and file-based inputs in social-auto-upload, which can still cause minor contention if the same files are reused, but the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same media directory, they may race on file selection or naming.
IF an external orchestrator adds write permissions, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Use separate working directories for notes and uploads.
Rename files before upload to avoid collisions.
Run one agent at a time on shared assets.
Keep git-managed content out of the uploader path.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can generate retrieved answers from personal notes, and social-auto-upload can act on file-based inputs and external APIs. If Khoj output is treated as authoritative by the uploader workflow, a mistaken summary or hallucinated metadata can cascade into incorrect uploads or captions. No verification step is documented between them.
conditions: IF Khoj-generated text is used as the source of titles, captions, or tags, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF social-auto-upload is configured to auto-publish without human review, errors propagate immediately.
mitigations: Require human review of Khoj output before upload.
Compare generated captions against source media metadata.
Use a draft-only publishing mode.
Add a checklist for title, tags, and destination account.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media for multiple social platforms. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if personal or regulated content is moved from a note store into a third-party upload pipeline. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls.
conditions: IF personal notes contain regulated or jurisdiction-bound content and are exported into social-auto-upload, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF either agent retains logs longer than the other, deletion/export requests may not propagate consistently.
mitigations: Avoid uploading regulated content through the pair.
Check retention settings in both systems.
Use synthetic or public test data for uploads.
Document where account data and notes are stored.
